candidate.capability_basis: Official card identifies an instruction-tuned code model with code reasoning and agent-oriented training; this does not demonstrate stronger memory lifecycle/task performance than the existing general model.

rationale: A separately pretrained stock instruction model at the same admitted architecture and size is a legitimate next engineering experiment after retained instruction-following failures. It changes the inference input model, not the DML task oracle, memory truth or action-selection rules.

The configuration admits all338 expected tensors and1,543,714,304 parameters under unchanged bounds. This establishes metadata compatibility only; no learned tensor byte, dtype, finiteness, source payload or actual consumer load is verified by the count calculation.

The candidate can reuse CPU/F32/eager execution, native template, request-local cache, syntax-only grammar and the existing policy/tool descriptions. No stronger memory or lifecycle competence is asserted from its name or code-oriented training.

Any qualifying outcome would apply to the explicitly pinned model and declared bounded campaign. Failed original-model runs remain failures; eventual model selection is not an unseen-workload quality comparison or evidence that DML beats a baseline.
required_before_next_campaign: Finish the entire active attempt5 and both sequential replays; preserve raw successes, conflicts, timeouts and all historical source/model identities before releasing the freeze.

Review an explicit second exact-source preparation entry point/version. Keep original model/revision/pins and rejection behavior, with no caller-supplied trust hashes, arbitrary model selector, widened architecture bounds or consumer fallback.

Freeze the selected built-in source profile at call entry. Provenance must hash every module that defines source pins or normalization if implementation is split; one common safe pipeline may be reused.

Verify complete pinned source payloads, including tokenizer configuration and actual safetensors; all338 learned tensors must have exact expected names/shapes, CPU BF16 dtype, finite values, exact BF16-to-F32-to-BF16 bytes and verified serialized output digests.

Review and execute storage preparation only after all current workers/replays close; measure sufficient disk and memory headroom before downloads and normalization, preserve historical paths/content and all private-copy admission guarantees.

Independently grade code at least9.5, validate required final source, produce new trained provenance and zero-generation strict admission, and declare new model/source identity before any corpus generation.

Freeze the identical nine tasks/order, current policy/tool descriptions, grammar/parser/verifiers, greedy/cache/runtime pins, limits and acceptance gates. Run every task once, retain every failure and independently replay the complete campaign. Do not select per-task successful outputs or probe hidden corpus answers.
scope: Read-only model-selection and storage-plan assessment. This is not preparer code acceptance, model admission, trained outcome qualification or permission to mutate the active frozen campaign.

source_confirmation_boundary.fresh_model_card_and_config_web_access: Unavailable through browsing; no successful fresh retrieval is claimed. Configuration checks used the retained revision-pinned metadata assessment.
source_confirmation_boundary.tokenizer_config_sha256: Must be obtained and pinned before preparation.

storage_plan_review.mandatory_before_download: Measured available disk must cover two actual pinned raw payloads plus two expected F32 payloads, all metadata/copy overhead and1GiB reserve. Abort if insufficient.
storage_plan_review.preserved_boundary: Same-filesystem verified readonly source-blob hardlink and atomic replacement of only the duplicate historical path; both historical inventories/bytes remain available. Never deduplicate private consumer snapshots.
storage_plan_review.recovery: Before atomic replacement both originals remain; after it both paths refer to verified retained bytes. Unexpected identities or cleanup errors are retained explicitly, with no broad deletion.
